current_answer: For the September 15–16 FOMC decision, the directly observed Polymarket contract displayed 81% for a 25-basis-point increase and 20% for no change when accessed at 13:34 UTC on September 11. Against the matched 19:08 UTC snapshot on September 10, the named increase row was 18 percentage points higher and the no-change row 17 points lower. BLS had released August CPI at 08:30 ET: CPI-U rose 0.4% in August and 3.4% over 12 months, while CPI excluding food and energy rose 0.3% in the month and 2.4% over 12 months. The pool did not capture a contract quote at the release, so that sequence does not show why the price changed. A current CME FedWatch percentage was not captured because the embedded grid could not be directly accessed.

summary: Polymarket’s September contract displayed 81% for a 25 bp increase and 20% for no change when accessed September 11, 2026, 13:34 UTC.
Against the matched 19:08 UTC snapshot on September 10, the named increase row rose 18 percentage points and the no-change row fell 17 points; this is a measured change, not proof of a cause.
BLS reported August CPI-U up 0.4% in the month and 3.4% over 12 months; CPI excluding food and energy rose 0.3% in August and 2.4% over 12 months.
The September 15–16 FOMC meeting, associated with a Summary of Economic Projections, is next.
CME FedWatch remains separately labelled and unquoted because its embedded grid was not directly accessible in this check.
uncertainty: Polymarket did not display a separate quote timestamp; the 13:34 UTC access time is not a closing quote.
Displayed outcome rows include rounded small outcomes and should not be forced into an exact 100% distribution.
CME FedWatch’s live outcome grid was not directly accessible, so no current futures-implied percentage or cross-market spread is reported.
The pool did not capture a quote immediately before or after the CPI release, so CPI is not established as the cause of the observed contract movement.
CPI is one official release and the Committee’s decision remains ahead.
